newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Lack of fertiliser threatens Nigeria harvests.
newsitem.headline: Lack of fertiliser threatens Nigeria harvests.

text.p: Nigerian farmers have warned that prospects of poor harvests this year are being made worse by their inability to obtain fertiliser following the withdrawal of state subsidies.
Farmers had resorted to organic manure, which may not be good enough, Murtala Nyako, president of the Practising Farmers Association of Nigeria, told reporters in the capital Abuja.
He was speaking after a meeting with military ruler General Sani Abacha and state military administrators to discuss the looming emergency.
A 50kg bag of fertiliser, which used to sell at a subsidised price of 150 naira, now sells for 1,500 naira.
No statement was issued at the end of the meeting although it is due to reconvene on Monday.
"It is now becoming too late," said Balarabe Musa, a former governor of the northern Kaduna State and now a farmer.
"I have my fears, and it is real, this year's harvest is going to be the worst in the nation's history," he told Tempo weekly newspaper.
